title: A closed subset with empty fibre disappears after shrinking
statement: Let g : P → T be a locally finite type, quasi-compact morphism of schemes. Let y ∈ T and C ⊆ P be closed, with g⁻¹({y}) ∩ C = ∅. There is an ambient open V ⊆ T containing y such that g⁻¹(V ∩ closure({y})) and C are disjoint.

source.place: Tag 054W (Lemma 37.24.1), empty generic fibre; Tag 055N, reduction to the reduced closure of a point

proof.text: Put D = C ∩ g⁻¹(closure {y}), a closed subset of P. Construct its reduced induced subscheme W as the subscheme of Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal D. Mathlib IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal_coe_support and range_subschemeι identify the image of its inclusion i with D; the inclusion is quasi-compact by the existing subschemeι instance. Hence j = i ≫ g is quasi-compact. This constructs W directly; no data is chosen from an unproved existence theorem.

Suppose y lies in closure(range j). Apply lem-sc-picard-closure-specialization, the already proved AlgebraicGeometry.exists_specializes_of_mem_closure_range, to obtain x in W with j(x) specializing to y. Since i(x) belongs to D, j(x) belongs to closure {y}, so y specializes to j(x). The underlying space of T is T0; antisymmetry of specialization therefore gives j(x) = y. But i(x) belongs to C, contradicting g⁻¹({y}) ∩ C = ∅. Thus y is outside closure(range j).

Take V = T \ closure(range j). It is open and contains y. If x belongs to C and g(x) belongs to V ∩ closure {y}, then x belongs to D. The range identity for i supplies z in W with i(z) = x. Consequently g(x) = j(z) belongs to range j and thus its closure, contradicting g(x) in V. This proves the required disjointness, including the empty C and empty D cases without a separate branch.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_open_generic_fibre_closed_avoidance {P T : Scheme.{u}} (g : P ⟶ T)
    [LocallyOfFiniteType g] [QuasiCompact g] (y : T) (C : Set P)
    (hC : IsClosed C) (hempty : g ⁻¹' {y} ∩ C = ∅) :
    ∃ V : Set T, IsOpen V ∧ y ∈ V ∧ Disjoint (g ⁻¹' (V ∩ closure {y})) C
